scope: Reusable official Web UI host lifecycle/traversal and legacy projected source-over/same-size resource updates. No gameplay rules, game files, existing player pages/saves/servers or renderer selection changed.

ui: Canvas validates and projects once per content change and privately shares prepared leaves with its pointer router; content-based dirty detection still catches in-place edits.
Scroll uses its first projection unless reset/anchoring changes effective offsets. Text input freshly scans current node kinds and returns the original snapshot when no fields exist.

Disposed handles release retained trees, serialized content, usage, pointer ownership and editing listeners. Retired virtual lists release keys and suppress queued post-lifetime requests; in-flight callbacks capture scalar request fields.
projected: Opt-in source_over requires host raster and both depth flags false. Default opaque/cutout behavior remains; source-over retains one authored order/id queue behind Canvas HUD.

Linear source-over filtering interpolates premultiplied encoded or linear texels and restores straight RGB before explicit SrcAlpha blending. Full-alpha 2D use sets cutoff0; the advanced API default remains0.05.

Presentation-owned decoder keys both complete packed strings, both counts and revision, validates metadata each draw, retains one accepted generation and rejects stale invalid payloads. Default public geometry results are detached.

Same-sized vertex/index changes swap renderer-owned arrays and upload existing GPU buffers. Unchanged bytes/materials/callbacks reuse owners; failed staged commits restore previous buffers/materials/uniforms and retire new resources.
All new production behavior lives in already inventoried Web files; no new production module dependency was added.

webUnitSuite.finalSourceDelta: Final rerun includes the strict-equality guard that skips idempotent undo assignments. The earlier GPU run precedes that guard; geometry/shader/ownership behavior is unchanged and independent final source review found no P1/P2.

focusedUi.includes: Controlled --expose-gc child keeps four disposed public handles and an actually started unresolved virtual request alive, while WeakRefs confirm former rect/key graphs are released. This is not a real-game GC-frequency/heap soak.

canvasPixels.scope: Actual official Canvas pixels, TC translation adapter only; not original bitmap font or normal game acceptance

projectedPixels.scope: Actual official host-raster legacy projected adapter versus Canvas2D drawImage, full-frame RGB/RGBA pixels, existing GL buffer updates, stale-payload rejection and bounded resource retirement; no FPS or long-soak claim.

gpu.renderer: ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (0x00002C02) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)

independentReview.mode: Read-only Codex review of final current source including idempotent assignment guard
independentReview.reviewed: Full-string cache/metadata validation, borrowed/owned arrays, commit rollback/version reupload, disposal/context loss, order/depth, manual premultiplied sampling and crop/scissor orientation

performanceLimit: The current frozen JYRogue candidate3 remains below59 actual simulation ticks/s for detail-world idle/drag/travel after O3+UI hosts; see web-priority-candidate3-browser.json. Advanced projected source-over has not been measured on actual gameplay. The unshipped set2D preset was withdrawn; ADR0044 selects a retained-resource/instance direction without implementing new authoring/transport APIs. This evidence does not establish stable60FPS, no memory leak anywhere, or infrequent real-game GC.
samplingLimit: Canvas agreement is bounded to the twelve reported synthetic cases on the recorded Chromium/ANGLE/NVIDIA GPU, tolerance2/255 (nearest exact). No universal browser/backend pixel-exactness or arbitrary future atlas-crop guarantee is implied.
